name: noise and audio-rate filter texture lead
goal: Create a radioactive/unstable cinematic texture or lead: dual detuned saws + WT character, aftertouch bringing in a sharp high oscillator, and mod-wheel sending noise (~30% mix) into audio-rate-style filter modulation (plus optional Osc2→cutoff always-on grit).

source.title: TRAVELER Track Walkthrough by Venus Theory

prerequisites: Hybrid synth or Traveler-inspired Web Audio engine with multi-osc, stereo filter, envelopes, LFOs/mod matrix, sequenced control tracks (or automation), and FX (EQ/chorus/delay/reverb)

inputs.name: audio_rate_mod
inputs.description: Whether Osc2 continuously modulates LPF frequency

outputs.name: unstable_texture_patch
outputs.description: Spooky evolving texture/lead with noise-modulated filter

constraints: Original synthesis only; not affiliated with KeySolutions; do not rip Traveler samples/presets/wavetables.
Original synthesis only — design new patches from portable parameters; do not copy proprietary Traveler factory preset names, banks, wavetables, or samples.
Not affiliated with KeySolutions Sounds or Traveler; concepts mapped to generic hybrid-synth / Web Audio equivalents.
Do not rip, dump, or redistribute Traveler content.
Prefer recreating the described signal-flow and motion relationships in our browser music system or any hybrid synth with comparable modules.

steps.action: Layer two fairly separate saw oscillators plus a wavetable osc for character. Slightly detune one osc; further detune can yield ring-mod-like artifacts.
Optionally enable continuous Osc2 → low-pass cutoff (audio-rate-ish FM-of-filter) for granular grit; A/B it to hear the instability.
Mix noise around ~30%. Map mod wheel to send noise into LPF cutoff modulation — annihilating cutoff with noise yields extremely unstable/distorted color.
Use aftertouch (or pressure) to bring in a high-frequency oscillator for resonant overtones that feel like distortion byproducts when played low.
Play as lead, texture, or pre-scare sting; leave headroom — this patch is intentionally unstable.

verification: Mod wheel clearly increases noise→filter effect
